title: Coherence of exceptional Künneth transposes
statement:
Use the finite-field datum and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and the actual constructible operations of [sk-def-sf-operations], on separated finite-type $k$-schemes. For pairs of composable separated finite-type morphisms $X_i\xrightarrow{f_i}Y_i\xrightarrow{g_i}S_i$, let $P_f=Rf_!$, $G_f=Rf^!$, with composition comparisons conjugate to those of $P$. Let $\alpha_f$ be the Ku_!–counit transpose of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](ii). Under the composition identifications, for every $L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(S_i,A)$ one has
$$\alpha_{(g_1f_1,g_2f_2)}=(G_{f_1\times f_2}\alpha_{(g_1,g_2)})\circ\alpha_{(f_1,f_2)}(G_{g_1}L_1,G_{g_2}L_2).$$
For an identity pair the comparison is the identity; conjugating by product-swap and tensor symmetry identifies $\alpha_{(f_1,f_2)}$ with $\alpha_{(f_2,f_1)}$. These are equalities of the specified maps, without an invertibility assertion for $\alpha$.

source.place: alpha: composition and symmetry of the exceptional adjoint comparison implicit in affine factorization

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal C_Z=D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, $P_u=Ru_!$, $G_u=Ru^!$, and $t_f=\mathrm{Ku}_!(f_1,f_2)$. These are the actual constructible adjunctions of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi). The product adjunction $(P_{f_1},P_{f_2})\dashv(G_{f_1},G_{f_2})$ has the componentwise Hom bijection and componentwise counits. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] with $L_1=(P_{f_1},P_{f_2})$, $L_2=P_F$, and $G,H$ the external-product functors on the source and target pairs. Its transpose description is exactly [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](ii); thus its mate is the specified $\alpha_f$, rather than an arbitrary comparison. In particular, for $E_i\in\mathcal C_{Y_i}$ and $E=E_1\boxtimes E_2$,
$$\varepsilon_{F,E}\circ P_F(\alpha_f(E_1,E_2))=(\varepsilon_{f_1,E_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2,E_2})\circ t_f(G_{f_1}E_1,G_{f_2}E_2).$$
The adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so equality after this inverse transposition proves equality of the original morphisms.

Put $F=f_1\times f_2$, $G=g_1\times g_2$ and $h_i=g_if_i$. The left-adjoint input is [lem-sf-kv-shriek-composition]: under the specified composition identifications,
$$t_h(B_1,B_2)=t_g(P_{f_1}B_1,P_{f_2}B_2)\circ P_G(t_f(B_1,B_2)).$$
It also gives $t_{\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. This is a statement about the concrete compact-support product maps; it assumes no exceptional-product comparison. Its naturality in the two inputs is the naturality of the relative product map in [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] and of the base-change comparisons in its construction [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i).

source.place: alpha: left-adjoint composition input for affine factorization

proof.text:
Under the conjugate composition comparisons of the question, [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] identify the counits with
$$\varepsilon_{GF} =\varepsilon_G\circ P_G\varepsilon_FG_G,\qquad \varepsilon_{h_i}=\varepsilon_{g_i}\circ P_{g_i}\varepsilon_{f_i}G_{g_i}.$$
This follows from the displayed composite-counit formula and the definition of a conjugate comparison. Put $L=L_1\boxtimes L_2$, $E_i=G_{g_i}L_i$, $K_i=G_{f_i}E_i$, and $E=E_1\boxtimes E_2$. For $u=G_F(\alpha_g(L_1,L_2))\circ\alpha_f(E_1,E_2)$, inverse transposition under $P_GP_F\dashv G_FG_G$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{GF,L}\circ P_GP_F(u)
&=\varepsilon_{G,L}\circ P_G(\alpha_g)\circ P_G(\varepsilon_{F,E}\circ P_F\alpha_f)\\
&=(\varepsilon_{g_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{g_2})\circ t_g(E_1,E_2)\circ P_G((\varepsilon_{f_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2})\circ t_f(K_1,K_2))\\
&=((\varepsilon_{g_1}\circ P_{g_1}\varepsilon_{f_1})\boxtimes(\varepsilon_{g_2}\circ P_{g_2}\varepsilon_{f_2}))\circ t_g(P_{f_1}K_1,P_{f_2}K_2)\circ P_G(t_f(K_1,K_2))\\
&=(\varepsilon_{h_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{h_2})\circ t_h(K_1,K_2).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality is naturality of $\varepsilon_F$; the second is step 1 for $f,g$; the third is naturality of $t_g$ with respect to the two counits; the fourth is step 2 and the component composite-counit formula. The last line is the inverse transpose of $\alpha_h$ by step 1. Injectivity proves the composition equality.

source.place: alpha: explicit composite-counit calculation of the composition identity

proof.text: For an identity pair use the canonical identity comparisons for $P$, and their conjugates for $G$. The identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] has identity counit. By step 2, $t_{\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$, so the inverse transpose defining $\alpha$ in step 1 is the identity map of $L_1\boxtimes L_2$. Transposition for the identity adjunction is the identity function. This proves the identity assertion, also for arbitrary chosen exceptional adjoints after the specified conjugate identifications.

Let $\tau_X:X_2\times X_1\to X_1\times X_2$ and $\tau_Y:Y_2\times Y_1\to Y_1\times Y_2$ be the swap isomorphisms, $F=f_1\times f_2$ and $F'=f_2\times f_1$; then $F\tau_X=\tau_YF'$ and the square $(\tau_X,F',F,\tau_Y)$ is Cartesian. Write $s$ for the pullback-composition identification $L\tau^*(M_1\boxtimes M_2)\cong M_2\boxtimes M_1$ followed by the signed symmetry of $\otimes^L$ (on $X$ or on $Y$), and $e:L\tau_Y^*P_F\to P_{F'}L\tau_X^*$ for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of this square [sk-def-sf-exchanges]. First, for $B_i\in\mathcal C_{X_i}$,
$$s\circ L\tau_Y^*\,t_{f_1,f_2}(B_1,B_2)=t_{f_2,f_1}(B_2,B_1)\circ P_{F'}(s)\circ e.\qquad(*)$$
By [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i), $t_{f_1,f_2}$ is $\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{a,b}$ over $B=Y_1\times Y_2$, for $a=f_1\times\mathrm{id}_{Y_2}$ and $b=\mathrm{id}_{Y_1}\times f_2$, followed by the inverse exchanges $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of the two product squares over $f_1$ and $f_2$. The base-change clause (iii) of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] for $\tau_Y:Y_2\times Y_1\to B$ (a separated finite-type base) identifies $L\tau_Y^*\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{a,b}$ with $\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}$ of the base-changed maps, which are $\mathrm{id}_{Y_2}\times f_1$ and $f_2\times\mathrm{id}_{Y_1}$, through $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ along $\tau_Y$ for $a$, $b$ and $F$ (the last is $e$) and the monoidality of $L\tau_Y^*$. Its symmetry clause (i) then exchanges the two factors, with the swap of the fibre product and the Koszul signs of $\sigma$; this yields the $\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}$ in the construction of $t_{f_2,f_1}$. Finally the horizontal pasting equation of [fix-lem-exchanges](2), for the square along $\tau_Y$ pasted with the product square over $f_1$ (whose composite bottom map $\mathrm{pr}_{Y_1}\tau_Y$ is the projection $Y_2\times Y_1\to Y_1$), identifies $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ along $\tau_Y$ for $a$, followed by $L\tau_Y^*$ of the product-square exchange for $f_1$, with the product-square exchange for $f_1$ over $Y_2\times Y_1$; likewise for $f_2$. Substituting these identities gives $(*)$. These schemes are separated of finite type and all inputs lie in the finite-Tor categories of step 1, as these clauses require.

Now transpose. Apply $s\circ L\tau_Y^*(-)$ to the step-1 equation for $(f_1,f_2)$ at $E_i=L_i$. Naturality of the signed symmetry gives $s\circ L\tau_Y^*(\varepsilon_{f_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2})=(\varepsilon_{f_2}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_1})\circ s$, and $(*)$ with $B_i=G_{f_i}L_i$, followed by the step-1 equation for $(f_2,f_1)$, gives
$$s\circ L\tau_Y^*\bigl(\varepsilon_{F}\circ P_F\alpha_{(f_1,f_2)}(L_1,L_2)\bigr)=\varepsilon_{F'}\circ P_{F'}\bigl(\alpha_{(f_2,f_1)}(L_2,L_1)\circ s\bigr)\circ e .$$
The left side is, by the definition of the conjugate in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] for the composite adjunctions $L\tau_Y^*P_F\dashv G_FR\tau_{Y*}$ and $P_{F'}L\tau_X^*\dashv R\tau_{X*}G_{F'}$ of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] (here $L\tau^*\dashv R\tau_*$ are inverse equivalences), the transpose of $\alpha_{(f_1,f_2)}$ transported along the swap by $s$ and by the conjugate $e^c$ of $e$; the right side is the transpose of $\alpha_{(f_2,f_1)}\circ s$ composed with $e$. Hence the transported $\alpha_{(f_1,f_2)}$ and $\alpha_{(f_2,f_1)}\circ s$ have the same transpose, and transpose injectivity from step 1 proves the asserted symmetry. All symmetries retain their Koszul signs; no invertibility of $\alpha$ or of $e$ is used.

split_report.summary: Expanded the exceptional product coherence into its mate definition, a searched left-adjoint Ku_! composition input, the explicit composite-counit equality, identity normalization and signed swap. No invertibility of alpha and no optional ambient pro-etale adjoint is used. Added one genuine geometric left-adjoint comparison statement, not an exceptional coherence clause.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the alpha paragraph of sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier: the composition compatibility needed for affine factorization and the symmetric two-variable treatment.

tool_uses.why: Uses the actual relative product naturality, symmetry and base-change clauses to identify the left-adjoint Ku_! maps; these are generic product tools explicitly used in sk-def-sf-kv-maps, not a replacement of the alpha proof route.

Step 5 uses only the horizontal pasting equation of its clause (2) for Ex_! along the swap isomorphism composed with the product-square exchanges that build Ku_!; no node of sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier's own route states Ex_! pasting, and the unit's sibling nodes already use this generic tool.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N1-932842ade (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the mathematics. The item statement is byte-identical to the base and was not weakened. Two stmt_deps were added (thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate); both are justified by the statement's conjugate composition comparisons. Coefficients are A_{E,n} on D^b_ctf throughout, with the unconditional adjunction of sk-def-sf-operations(vi) and P from (iv). thm-sf-comp-composition, stated on D^+_et, restricts to these objects because constructible objects have étale origin. No Rf^x and no admissibility datum is used. Step 1: α is the mate in def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate of Ku_! for the componentwise product adjunction, and its transpose matches sk-def-sf-kv-maps(ii). Step 3: I checked all four lines of the counit calculation: naturality of ε_F, step 1 for g and f, naturality of t_g along ε_{f_i}, then the new node with B_i=K_i and the conjugate counit identity. Step 4: the identity pair is correct. Step 5 was mistyped (P_F where P_{F'} and the exchange along the swap are needed). It also covered the target identifications with 'base-change compatibility' (E5, C1/C4): it needs horizontal pasting of Ex_!. I rewrote step 5 with the precise equation (*) s∘Lτ_Y^* t_{f1,f2}=t_{f2,f1}∘P_{F'}(s)∘e. It is derived from sk-def-sf-kv-maps(i), the base-change clause (iii) along τ_Y and symmetry clause (i) of sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative, and the pasting clause (2) of fix-lem-exchanges, then transposed through the conjugate e^c for the composite adjunctions. Uses and proof_deps were updated. I accepted the tool uses sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative (Ku_! is built from κ^rel) and fix-lem-exchanges (already accepted in sibling nodes of this unit). The new node lem-sf-kv-shriek-composition is self-contained and statement-only. It concerns only the left-adjoint map t, so it is strictly smaller than the item and not a restated clause. It holds on the cases I tested (all identities, g=id, f2=g2=id, zero objects). It duplicates no node: sk-thm-sf-compatibility(6) and lem-sf-kunneth-coherence have no composition clause, and prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth proves the identity only inline. Its blueprint from/via are correct, there are no cycles, and the searches cover all three kinds.
